annotation.authors_or_issuer: Israel National Program for Artificial Intelligence (Ministry of Innovation, Science and Technology; Telem; Innovation Authority)
named_instruments_referenced: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI
annotation.summary_en: Israel's National AI Program strategy paper (April 2025) reviewing the global AI landscape and regulation, then setting five objectives: AI infrastructure and talent, high-tech adoption, safe AI in the public sector, global geo-technological standing, and ministry preparedness. It favors innovation-friendly, sandbox-based, internationally compatible regulation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Multi-year program (2021-2026) budgeted at about NIS 1 billion.
Five objectives: infrastructure/research, high-tech adoption, public-sector AI, global positioning, ministry preparation.
Regulatory sandboxes and innovation-supportive regulation compatible with international standards.
Establish cross-government regulatory knowledge center, regulators forum and expert advisory group.
Publish AI ethics and regulation policy principles paper; build disciplinary data assets with privacy safeguards.
